answer: Ferrous Beacon Handshake. Each agent must solve a hardware-tied challenge that embeds a unique ferrous-domain timing fingerprint into its first transaction; duplicates cannot share it without colliding. The ledger anchors every fingerprint to an ocean of rotating checkpoints, so a clone either forks the fingerprint (detectable) or waits for expiry. An attacker pays one physical timing source per identity plus re-sync at each vertex, making mass duplication cost linear in real hardware.
